test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A 248-m-long train travelling at 88 km/h takes 30 seconds to cross another train, x m long, travelling at 34 km/h in the same direction. What is the value of x ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same Direction) = 88 − 34 = 54 km/h

Convert to m/s: 54 × (5/18) = 15 m/s

Total Distance (Sum of lengths) = **Speed × Time** = 15 × 30 = 450 m

Value of x = Total Distance − Length of first train = 450 − 248 = 202 m

**∴ The correct answer is 202 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **Train 1** (L₁) = 248 m

Speed of **Train 1** (S₁) = 88 km/h

Length of **Train 2** (L₂) = x m

Speed of **Train 2** (S₂) = 34 km/h

**Time taken** to cross (T) = 30 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S₁ − S₂

Total Distance = Length₁ + Length₂

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f956b258d306dac12258882fd8f3e986c07bee1828fddc128ff62e29199960c1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 88 − 34 = 54 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 54 × (5/18) = 3 × 5 = 15 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = (248 + x) m

⇒ Total Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ 248 + x = 15 × 30

⇒ 248 + x = 450

⇒ x = 450 − 248

⇒ x = 202 m

**∴ The correct answer is 202 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the **same direction**, relative speed is (S₁ − S₂). When moving in the **opposite direction**, relative speed is (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by **5/18**. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by **18/5**.

Train Crossing Logic

When a train crosses another train, the **total distance** covered is always the sum of the lengths of both trains (L₁ + L₂).</p
